opex.note: Designing new data-infrastructure chips and platforms; up 43% YoY as hiring and stock pay rose.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling the chips and running the company; up 34% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring related charges (gains), net
opex.note: A small net gain (a credit) this quarter — items such as contract changes and property sales, net of severance and facility-exit costs, came out in Marvell's favor.

follow100Note: Communications and other takes $20.73 of every $100 and Data Center $79.27. The spending rows add to $99.99 rather than exactly $100.00 because each row is rounded to two decimals.
footerNote: Marvell reports revenue in two end markets: Data center, and Communications and other.
oneTimers: A net $52.0M fair-value loss sat inside interest and other loss, net: a $101.9M increase in the fair value of the contingent consideration owed for the Celestial acquisition, partly offset by a $49.9M unrealized gain on a forward stock purchase contract. Both are excluded from non-GAAP results.

GAAP profit is far below non-GAAP profit ($308.0M vs $865.9M) mainly because GAAP includes $326.2M of stock-based compensation and $214.9M of amortization of acquired intangible assets, both excluded from non-GAAP.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $61.6M plus other expense, net of $19.8M — a net $81.4M non-operating loss. Inside it, a $101.9M rise in the fair value of the Celestial acquisition contingent consideration was partly offset by a $49.9M gain on a forward stock purchase contract.

segments.name: Data center
segments.note: AI and cloud data-center chips — custom silicon, connectivity, ethernet switching and storage; up 46% YoY and 79% of all revenue.

segments.name: Communications and other
segments.note: Enterprise networking, carrier infrastructure, consumer and automotive/industrial chips, which Marvell now reports as one combined end market; up 10% YoY.

sources.label: Form 10-Q, incl. revenue disaggregation by end market (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit $2,171.5M, up 46% from a year ago and 18% from last quarter — 79% of all revenue. Marvell said AI-related bookings remain exceptionally robust and raised its outlook for fiscal 2027 and 2028.
takeaways.title: Data Center is carrying the growth

takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.33 against $0.94 non-GAAP. The gap is mostly $326.2M of stock-based compensation and $214.9M of amortization on past acquisitions, plus a net $52.0M fair-value loss tied to the Celestial deal — all real costs that non-GAAP leaves out.
takeaways.title: GAAP profit looks much smaller than non-GAAP

takeaways.text: Marvell guided Q3 FY27 revenue to $3.15B (±5%), with GAAP EPS of $0.53 (±$0.05) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.10 (±$0.05) — a big step up from this quarter's $2.74B as its Custom business accelerates.
takeaways.title: Next quarter is guided to another record

verdict: Marvell set another revenue record at $2.74B, up 37%, as Data Center sales jumped 46% to 79% of the business — but stock pay, acquisition amortization and a Celestial fair-value charge held GAAP profit to $308M, well below the $866M non-GAAP figure.
